policyCorrection: Polymer synthesis methodology is in scope when the central contribution is a new or substantially advanced polymerization reaction/catalyst/control strategy with general preparative relevance (for example monomer scope, controlled/living polymerization, sequence/architecture control, or access to previously inaccessible polymer structures). Exclude polymer/material papers when polymerization is merely a fabrication/application step or a one-off material transformation without a general preparative polymer-synthesis method.

accepted.title: Alternating Copolymerization of Arynes and Aldehydes Enabled by an N-Arylamine Initiator
accepted.titleZh: N-芳基胺引发的芳炔与醛交替共聚
accepted.reason: Central contribution is a new direct alternating copolymerization of arynes and aldehydes; the method suppresses aryne homopolymerization and enables block, cyclic, and ring-expansion polymer architectures.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Crossref publisher metadata/abstract states direct alternating copolymerization of arynes and aldehydes initiated by a simple N-arylamine, with a Smiles-type rearrangement propagation pathway and access to block copolymers, cyclic polymers, and ring-expansion alternating copolymerization.
accepted.challengeReason: Although the products are polymers, this is not a materials-performance paper: the polymerization reaction itself, chain-end regeneration, selectivity, and architecture control are the main scientific contribution.

accepted.title: Controlled Cationic Ring-Opening Polymerization Enables Chemically Recyclable Polyacetal-Based Polyurethanes
accepted.titleZh: 可控阳离子开环聚合实现化学可回收聚缩醛基聚氨酯
accepted.reason: Develops an anion-binding catalytic strategy for reversible-deactivation cationic ring-opening polymerization of cyclic acetals, enabling precision polymer synthesis at kilogram scale.
accepted.evidenceBasis: The Angew/PubMed abstract describes a highly efficient anion-binding catalytic polymerization strategy for reversible-deactivation cationic ring-opening polymerization, precision synthesis of poly(1,3-dioxepane) diol on kilogram scale, and downstream recyclable polyurethane synthesis.
accepted.challengeReason: The polyurethane application is downstream; the central enabling advance is a controlled polymerization methodology with scale, precision, and chemical recycling implications.

accepted.title: Fine Tuning of Catalyst Active Sites to Access Advanced Ultrahigh-Melting Polyolefins
accepted.titleZh: 精细调控催化剂活性位点合成先进超高熔点聚烯烃
accepted.reason: Develops a modified pyridylamido Hf catalyst active species that enables polymerization of sterically demanding bulky alpha-olefins and access to previously inaccessible polyolefin structures.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Wiley Early View states that precontacting the pyridylamido Hf catalyst with allyltrimethylsilane redesigns the active species and enables polymerization of sterically challenging bulky alpha-olefins to ultrahigh-melting polyolefins not previously produced.
accepted.challengeReason: The high melting point is a materials property, but the paper's enabling contribution is catalyst/active-site control that unlocks a previously inaccessible polymerization substrate class.
